title: We Love Katamari
subtitle: The fans ask for another roll
summary: We Love Katamari is Namco's PlayStation 2 action-puzzle sequel, first released in Japan on 7 July 2005. The King of All Cosmos now receives requests from admirers of the previous game, sending the Prince out with his adhesive katamari to satisfy them. Rolling over objects makes the ball grow until things that once blocked its path become part of it. The sequel keeps that simple action while changing what each assignment asks the player to collect, where to roll and how success is measured.
body: We Love Katamari is Namco's PlayStation 2 action-puzzle sequel, first released in Japan on 7 July 2005. The King of All Cosmos now receives requests from admirers of the previous game, sending the Prince out with his adhesive katamari to satisfy them. Rolling over objects makes the ball grow until things that once blocked its path become part of it. The sequel keeps that simple action while changing what each assignment asks the player to collect, where to roll and how success is measured.

Different requests reshape the same rolling controls. An objective may emphasise a certain kind of object or put the Prince in surroundings that change the route through a stage. Size remains the basic language: a small ball squeezes between familiar household things, while a larger one absorbs parts of the environment that seemed fixed moments earlier. The player learns each place by the order in which it becomes collectible. These changes give individual tasks a character without requiring a different set of controls for every challenge.

Keita Takahashi returned to direct after initially resisting another Katamari game. The fans appearing inside it turn that real pressure for more into part of the fiction. Multiplayer includes both competition and cooperative rolling, asking two people to coordinate the movement of one ball. A varied soundtrack again accompanies the shifts in scale and setting. The 2023 Reroll+ Royal Reverie remaster brought the adventure to later platforms, while the original remains the second Katamari game and the last in the series directed by Takahashi.
